title: LEFT JOIN and Finding Missing Rows

contentBlocks.body: LEFT (OUTER) JOIN keeps every row from the left table. Where the ON condition finds matches, you get one row per match, exactly like an inner join. Where it finds none, you still get the left row once, with NULL in every column from the right table. RIGHT JOIN is the mirror image and is rarely used; FULL OUTER JOIN keeps unmatched rows from both sides.

contentBlocks.code:
-- Every customer, with how many orders they placed (0 for none)
SELECT c.id, c.name,
       COUNT(o.id)                AS order_count,  -- NOT COUNT(*)
       COALESCE(SUM(o.total), 0)  AS total_spent
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY c.id;

contentBlocks.body: Why COUNT(o.id) and not COUNT(*)? A customer with no orders still produces one joined row (with o.id NULL). COUNT(*) counts that row and reports 1; COUNT(o.id) skips the NULL and correctly reports 0. For the same reason SUM(o.total) is NULL for them, so COALESCE it to 0.

contentBlocks.code:
-- Bug: the WHERE runs after the join and throws away the NULL rows,
-- silently turning the LEFT JOIN into an INNER JOIN
SELECT c.name, o.id
FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.status = 'paid';

-- Fix: filter the right table inside ON
SELECT c.name, o.id
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id AND o.status = 'paid';

-- Anti-join: customers with no orders at all
SELECT c.id FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.id IS NULL;              -- or: WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id)

knowledgeItems.prompt: Model the first query in the lesson: every customer (ordered by id) with orderCount = COUNT(o.id) and totalSpent = COALESCE(SUM(o.total), 0). Return objects with keys id, name, orderCount, totalSpent in that order.
`FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.status = 'paid'` no longer returns customers without orders. Why?

choices: status must be indexed for LEFT JOIN to work
For unmatched customers o.status is NULL, so the WHERE predicate is UNKNOWN and the row is removed
payload.answer: For unmatched customers o.status is NULL, so the WHERE predicate is UNKNOWN and the row is removed
payload.explanation: WHERE runs after the join. Move the condition into the ON clause to filter which orders match while still keeping every customer.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Customer 5 has no orders. What does `SELECT c.id, COUNT(*) FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id` report for customer 5?

choices: Customer 5 is not in the result
payload.explanation: The left join still produces one row for customer 5 (with NULL order columns), and COUNT(*) counts rows. Use COUNT(o.id) to count only real matches.
